components.visible: A short upright segment at far upper left bends right into an approximately horizontal dark handle ending at the upper central drive. Preserve the visible bend; it is not a detached straight bar.

One broad, irregular dark transverse grip at the top of the central drive, with white specks/short gaps. Grip and bent handle overlap at the central dark junction; separate hidden fastening surfaces cannot be seen.
A short vertical shaft with alternating black and white diagonal/ring-like bands descends from the top grip to a collar.
Flattened oval/ring-like collar on the top crosspiece, with a dark lower front edge and small white interior openings.

A narrow oblique perspective crosspiece joins the two vertical frame supports. It has distinct top and front edges, a raised dark left fastener near x73,y120 and a raised dark right fastener near x198,y111.
A freestanding B-like glyph to the right of the upper shaft; silhouette visible. Latin versus a lookalike script is not determined from pixels.

uncertainty: Thread/ring boundaries in the upper shaft merge into the grip and collar; a uniquely counted set of hidden turns is not available.
White specks in the grip are visible raster details, not evidence of a particular screw or hole topology.

components.visible: Left vertical support with a thin outer edge and a much darker inner/front strip. It runs from the top crosspiece toward the lower base. The adjacent marked strip and support overlap; they are not two unrelated rulers.

Right nearly vertical support descends from the top crosspiece into/behind the upper elliptical plate. A hose arch occludes part of it near y207-232. Small dark fleck left of the support near x190,y159 is visible but has no independently recoverable mechanical role.

A vertical closely spaced diagonal/ring-patterned screw between the frame supports. Its visible patterned portion begins immediately below the top crosspiece and ends at the upper plate collar. Do not replace it with a smooth rod.
The lower drive enters a small pedestal/collar on the upper plate; dark rim and white interior strips are visible. The adjacent hose endpoint is to its right.

uncertainty: The top and bottom screw-pattern segments touch crosspiece/collar ink, so an exact thread-turn count is not uniquely recoverable from these pixels.
The image supplies exterior contacts and occlusions, not internal drive, bearing, or fastener construction.

components.visible: A narrow vertical marked strip lies along the left support. An outlined longer rectangular/guide-like feature runs on its right in the upper portion and ends near y294. The upper slanted boundary near y209 joins the dark support.
One separate L-like italic glyph to the left, level with the upper plate.

markInventory.certainSpatialPattern: Several short dark strokes slope downward to the right across the light strip. They are real visible marks, not permission to generate an arbitrary regular scale.

edgeOrOcclusionGroups.visible: Upper slanted border/support contact; whether a separate endpoint graduation is present cannot be separated.
Stroke-level dark material meets the upper plate rim/guide boundary; border versus an additional graduation cannot be uniquely partitioned.
Lower sloping stroke merges into support and base/plate contours.
Short dark spot/stroke near the foot and thick support edge; classification as a final graduation, fastener, or border detail is unresolved.

uncertainty: The listed clear strokes do not establish the complete graduation count: the upper boundary, plate-rim crossing, and foot contain inseparable dark groups.
No legible ruler numeral series or unit inscription can be independently recovered here.

components.visible: One broad perspective ellipse above the ribbed body; thin rear arc, thicker front lip, central drive collar, hose endpoint to its right, and frame supports are distinguishable. The rear arc is interrupted by the drive and hose.

A short cylindrical/bellows-like body with two side boundaries and a sequence of stacked, curved approximately horizontal contour bands. The lines bend with the cylindrical front; this is not a smooth generic vessel.

Curved line bands occupy approximately y319,328,338,348,358,369,379,389 and the dark lower-edge region around y399. These are positional bands, not a certified total fold count; endpoint bands merge into top/bottom rims and side supports.
Flattened oval bottom plate with a light upper rim and thick dark front/lower rim. A small raised/fleck-like dark feature appears on the right near x214,y402.

A dark protruding rounded foot below the front-left base near x105,y430; dark base/support material toward the left; broad dark underside toward the right. A dark band/white gap appears along the lower body/front just above the base. Do not infer hidden rear feet.

uncertainty: The source exterior can be inventoried as ribbed, but rim-connected contour endpoints do not provide a uniquely certified fold count.
No visible sectional view permits an internal cylinder, piston, sealing, or volume calibration claim.

components.visible: Dark short upright endpoint on the upper plate immediately right of the central drive foot. The hose rises out of this area.
Broad hose arches up and right from the plate, passes in front of the right support, crests around x213-227,y209-219, then descends toward x285-294,y327.

The descending hose makes a narrow low rounded bight around x276,y397-402 and returns upward/right. White interior space and black outer contours in the source crop support a continuous bend, not a detached endpoint.
Return run rises rightward toward the gauge connector, flattening around x375-423,y279-295. White highlight/gaps and irregular dark outer edges remain visible.
Narrow coupling/ring-like shapes join the hose to the left side of the gauge's vertical stem. Visible exterior contact only.

regions.topologyConclusion: One visible continuous external hose route from left upper plate, over the arch, around the low bight, and up to the gauge stem. No second hose or tee is required by the visible contours.
uncertainty: Internal lumen and connector construction are not shown. This does not justify adding a hidden tee, valve passage, or joint.
White highlight speckling is not an independent collection of pressure or calibration marks.

components.visible: One near-round housing, slightly perspective-oval, with a very thick dark outer rim, white/black edge flecks, and a light inner face. An isolated light patch interrupts the upper-right rim near x495,y114.

A segmented curved graduation band starts on the left near y173, follows the upper-left/top arc, then descends the right and lower-right side. On the upper-left it has outlined light compartments separated by short dark radial bars; on the right it merges into thick face/rim ink.

One dark diagonal pointer with a broad southwest tail, a central dark hub around x459,y173, and a narrow northeast-directed tip reaching the scale near x487,y142. No separately readable numeric position is asserted.
One freestanding M-like glyph to the right of the dial.

scaleAndGlyphInventory.visible: Small outlined arc compartments at the left start and a rounded dark/white loop-like glyph inside the face near x429,y171. A horizontal/oblique stroke touches the scale start; its separation from an endpoint graduation is not certain.

Individually visible light compartments/short radial bars ascend the upper-left arc. Their lower start and upper transition share border ink; visible segmentation is real but a complete tick-versus-cell-boundary enumeration is not unique.
A vertical dark stroke and neighboring bent/loop-like dark fragment(s) inside the upper-left scale. Their glyph grouping cannot be uniquely read.
Several bent, hooked and short upright dark fragments beneath the top arc; nearby graduation ink touches some of them.
Bent/hooked dark face fragments, radial/border material, and the pointer tip converge in the upper-right. The existence and position of ink are visible; exact glyph and tick separation is not.

Thick connected outer graduation/border material and several irregular inner hook/stroke groups on the right. They touch one another and the dark rim. Missing white separation cannot be reconstructed.
Further slanted inner stroke clusters and broad stepped/compartment-like black shapes follow the lower-right arc. Some contours merge into the housing border.
One broad V/hook-like connected dark cluster near the bottom interior. Whether it is a numeral, symbol, or merged glyph parts is unresolved.
Two vertically separated small dark fragments in the lower-left face, above the inner lower rim. They are not a recoverable unit inscription.

uncertainty: Complete graduation count, major/minor classification, and glyph identities cannot be uniquely recovered, especially on the upper-right through lower-right arc.
Do not regularize the scale, supply conventional gauge numerals, omit the crowded fragments, or count housing-border steps as certified graduations.
Pointer direction is visible geometry only. Its numeric reading, units, range, pressure reference, and absolute-versus-gauge interpretation remain unavailable.

components.visible: A small oval/ring-like neck below the dial leads into a vertical dark stem with light edge slivers; the stem continues toward the stand.
Ring/hexagon-like exterior fitting at the hose-to-stem contact.

Ring/hexagon-like exterior fitting at the right of the stem and one short roughly horizontal projection ending in a rounded dark tip. Small inner white/dark contours are visible; internal valve construction is not.
Dark central mount beneath the stem, with short white interior gaps and a raised/rounded dark lobe to its left.
One diagonal leg toward the lower left ending in a rounded dark foot.
One broad leg toward the lower right with light upper-edge strips and a rounded/blunt downward end.
An additional upper/right branch/edge projects behind or above the broad right leg. Its visible extent is bounded; hidden rear-leg geometry or an independent rear foot cannot be inferred.

uncertainty: The stem, hose coupling, right projection, central mount, and visible stand branches are positionally recoverable as exterior geometry.
No hidden port routing or fastener internals are shown. The upper/right branch does not certify a fully visible separate third foot.

regions.visible: No second panel, plotted axes, legend, standalone numerical caption, or physical unit block is visible. Small isolated background flecks include the lower center around x224,y430, x236,y445 and x271,y461; these are not promoted to apparatus or scale glyphs.
regions.uncertainty: Raster flecks are retained as observations, not interpreted as hidden components or measurement data.

sourceOnlyConclusion.reason: Gross exterior apparatus and hose layout are visible, but required dial graduation/glyph boundaries and ruler endpoint/occlusion marks remain non-unique. Pixel magnification reveals existing ink only and cannot resolve merged source marks.
